items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The increase in the proportion of a population living in urban areas"?
items.answer: urbanisation
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of urbanisation.

items.stem: Explain why the urban heat island effect is strongest on calm, clear nights.
items.answer: Buildings and roads release stored daytime heat slowly; with clear skies rural areas cool rapidly by radiation, while calm air means no wind mixes cooler rural air into the city, so the urban-rural difference is greatest.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Buildings and roads release stored daytime heat slowly; with clear skies rural areas cool rapidly by radiation, while calm air means no wind mixes cooler rural air into the city, so the urban-rural difference is greatest. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between urbanisation and urban growth.
items.answer: Urbanisation is an increase in the proportion of people living in urban areas; urban growth is an increase in the absolute urban population or area, which can occur without urbanisation if rural populations grow equally.
items.markingKey: Urbanisation is an increase in the proportion of people living in urban areas; urban growth is an increase in the absolute urban population or area, which can occur without urbanisation if rural populations grow equally. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Omar writes: "Cities have a lower environmental impact per person than rural areas in every respect." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Dense cities often have lower per-capita transport and heating energy, but higher consumption, imported resources and concentrated pollution; it depends on the city's wealth and design.
items.markingKey: Dense cities often have lower per-capita transport and heating energy, but higher consumption, imported resources and concentrated pollution; it depends on the city's wealth and design. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "urban heat island"?
options: A layer of warm air above cooler air near the ground that prevents vertical mixing and traps pollutants
Removal of sulfur dioxide from power-station exhaust gases, usually by reaction with limestone
A device that removes particulates from exhaust gases using an electrical charge
The higher air and surface temperatures of a city compared with surrounding rural areas, caused by dark surfaces, buildings, waste heat and lack of vegetation
items.answer: The higher air and surface temperatures of a city compared with surrounding rural areas, caused by dark surfaces, buildings, waste heat and lack of vegetation
items.markingKey: D. "urban heat island" is the higher air and surface temperatures of a city compared with surrounding rural areas, caused by dark surfaces, buildings, waste heat and lack of vegetation.

items.stem: State two differences between counter-urbanisation and suburbanisation.
items.answer: Counter-urbanisation is movement of people from urban areas to rural areas beyond the city; suburbanisation is movement from the inner city to the suburbs at the city's edge.
items.markingKey: Counter-urbanisation is movement of people from urban areas to rural areas beyond the city; suburbanisation is movement from the inner city to the suburbs at the city's edge. [1] per valid, explicit comparison up to [3].

items.stem: The urban agglomeration population of Dhaka grew from about 7.5 million in 1993 to about 23.2 million in 2023. (a) Calculate the mean annual growth rate. (b) Assuming this rate continues, project the population in 2033. (c) Explain two environmental problems that this growth creates for the urban system and one sustainable planning response.
items.answer: (a) (23.2/7.5)^(1/30) − 1 ≈ 3.8% per year (b) 23.2 × (1 + 0.038)^10 ≈ 33.8 million (c) e.g. air pollution from traffic and industry, inadequate sewage and solid-waste collection, urban heat island, loss of wetlands and farmland to sprawl, water shortages; responses: bus rapid transit (Lagos BRT), compact growth, green infrastructure, upgraded sanitation.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 compound growth formula, A1 3.8%. (b) A1 ≈ 33.8. (c) R1 R1 problems, R1 response.

items.stem: With reference to the resource booklet and examples you have studied, evaluate the claim: "Urbanisation is beneficial for the environment."
items.answer: Urbanisation can reduce per-capita impact if cities are dense and well planned, but rapid unplanned growth and high consumption usually increase environmental pressure.
items.markingKey: Strengths / supporting points: higher density lowers per-capita land and transport energy; efficient service provision; lower fertility in cities. Limitations / counter-points: concentrated pollution and waste; loss of farmland and habitats at the edges; high consumption and ecological footprint of urban residents; heat islands. Conclusion: Urbanisation can reduce per-capita impact if cities are dense and well planned, but rapid unplanned growth and high consumption usually increase environmental pressure. items.stem: Explain why a temperature inversion makes air pollution worse.
